newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine stocks close lower in muted session.
newsitem.headline: Argentine stocks close lower in muted session.

text.p: Argentine stocks limped to a lower close Wednesday in slack volume, undercut by fresh uncertainty surrounding a tax reform package, dealers said.
"The market is very hesitant -- there's no hard news to latch onto," said Jose Napoli of Ignoto y Napoli traders.
The MerVal index slumped after a powerful rally Tuesday, closing off 0.9 percent at 510.15.

Traders said prices were hurt by news the budget committee of Congress' lower house backed the government's tax bills but failed to scrap a clause forcing the central administration to share revenue from fuel tax hikes with the provinces.
"We don't want to jump to conclusions. But if this means the old revenue-sharing scheme remains in force then it's very bad news," said an emerging markets investment banker.

The budget committee's approval was anxiously awaited by the markets to clear the way for floor debate of the revenue-boosting package, which could happen as early as next Wednesday but more likely in 15 days.

Traders said investors would now have to wait for the Senate to pass a measure allowing the government to keep all of the new tax revenue and not hand over 71 percent, or around $1.0 billion, to the provinces.
"The charts show the MerVal could slide to a floor of 480. But it will probably be stuck in a tight band of 500-525, with very selective bidding and very little volume," said Napoli.
Stockpickers in the session singled out pulp and paper maker Celulosa, which jumped 3.5 percent on the back of bold positioning in the issue by a foreign buyer, dealers said.
Floor volume picked up slightly to 13.9 million pesos from 13.1 million Tuesday, while over-the-counter deals swelled to 116.6 million pesos against 89.6 million Tuesday.
The broad market closed off 1.0 percent, with losers beating winners 24 to 12 and 13 stocks closing flat.
Top main-tier gainers after Celulosa were sugar refiner Ledesma, up 1.8 percent, and Bansud bank, up 0.5 percent.
MerVal losses were led by agricultural holding company Cresud, Telefonica and construction stock Polledo, which shed 2.9 percent, 2.5 percent and 2.2 percent, respectively.

A MerVal stock exchange seat was also sold in the session to broker Juan Carlos Rodriguez by Comafi Bursatil for $550,000 -- a 22 percent rise since the last dollar sale of a bolsa seat on February 21. In the last peso sale July 4 a seat fetched 510,000 pesos.
